prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1419; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a second vehicle that entered on a late yellow. Police report requested. Claimant reported neck and back strain at scene and was transported to an urgent care facility. Liability appears disputed pending review of signal timing and witness statements.

Entry 2: Claimant is represented by counsel. Letter of representation received and logged. All further contact to be routed through the attorney's office. Requested medical authorization and prior treatment records for the cervical and lumbar spine. Reserve set at the initial estimate for bodily injury and property damage.

Entry 3: Spoke with defense counsel regarding the scene photographs and the intersection camera footage. Footage from the nearby business has been requested but retention period may have passed. Vehicle inspection completed. Damage consistent with a lateral impact to the driver door and rear quarter panel. Total loss evaluation scheduled.

Entry 4: Medical records received from urgent care. Diagnosis listed as acute cervical and lumbar strain with muscle spasm. Follow-up with a physical therapist ordered. Attorney's office indicated the claimant has missed two scheduled therapy visits and is awaiting a treatment plan. Noted for medical bill review.

Entry 5: Reviewed liability position with supervisor. Comparative fault analysis still open as the other driver disputes the signal phase. Recommended holding the bodily injury evaluation until the treatment course is documented and the signal timing records are obtained. Diary set for follow-up with counsel in two weeks.
